scope: Original planning envelope only; S2 integration requirements and exact gap inventory, not a new approved implementation packet

architecture.hexagonal: UI/native input → authenticated M04 application boundary → DocumentSession; HOST → approved codec abstraction + current FileCommitPort ← adapters
architecture.ownership: S1 DocumentSession owns content/history/baselines. IO owns native transaction scratch. Codec is a projection, not owner. Proposed HOST IO-health guard must be explicitly approved before new state exists.
architecture.transaction: capture R + semantic A → validate/encode bytes → capture raw E + expected disk D → current IO lease/commit receipt → trusted proof validation → acknowledge captured R/A if still applicable; preserve proof on late ACK failure
forbidden: raw digest used as semantic baseline
HOST deletes IO private recovery/scratch artifacts
domain state rebuilt just to set RecoveryRequired
fallback to write_atomic/create_dir_all for new formal transaction
implicit multi-file save/embedded design dual write

facts.fact: Accepted M04-S1 pure DocumentSession remains in source; capture returns document/session/revision/DocumentContent. Formal and recovery acknowledgement are separate APIs. Constructors are structural input seams, not trusted codec validation.
IO-PREREQ adapter is implemented and locally accepted, not an unimplemented marker. Fresh IO220 regression was recorded by M01-S2 delivery. Windows11/reparse/8.3 gates remain independent.
scene_doc.rs saves/loads text via FileSystemPort; source existence and its text roundtrip test do not validate a full lossless ESS work/architecture/design canonical codec.

Current uidesign_doc.rs drops UI-owned fields in existing controlled probe; M03 C1 preservation contract is proposed, not adopted or implemented. Cannot assume it supplies a complete M04 DocumentCodecPort.

CommitReceipt exposes target_path/previous_digest/committed_digest/transaction_id only. RecoveryRequired exposes exact diagnostic paths. IO owns OS handles/private scratch/version/journal representation.

findings.trigger: Historical storage proposal describes M04-level document-versions/document-transactions paths, whereas current accepted IO adapter owns private version/journal mechanics and success receipt does not expose an old-version handle.
findings.required_behavior: Single formal file commit with verified rollback/recovery semantics, no competing persistence authority.
findings.missing: Explicit current M04 consumer contract distinguishing IO private recovery artifacts from any separate user-facing retention requirement.
findings.recommendation: Consume actual FileCommitPort without duplicating its private journal. Keep original retention path proposal historical, not a new write target. If long-term document version history is required, propose it separately with its own approved lifecycle/Port rather than silently implementing it.

findings.trigger: DocumentCodecPort proposal still names DocumentFormat/CodecError and full-document canonicalization/preservation responsibilities without fully frozen types, exact per-format field exclusions and complete codec fixture/error oracle mapping.
findings.required_behavior: Full ESS composite document or standalone .sgendesign must preserve supported content or reject before write.
findings.missing: Precise ESS XML profile, .sgendesign dependency/adoption contract, semantic canonical payload versus raw persisted bytes, actual codec-owned error shape.
findings.recommendation: Prepare one exact codec/type/error/field-map package. Reuse M03 only after its contract is adopted; do not treat scene text helper or packet read-only extraction as full serializer. Do not implement the absent codec adapter from placeholder names.

findings.trigger: WORK acknowledge_formal_save expects semantic digest, while CommitReceipt.committed_digest hashes exact encoded file bytes. The two may legitimately differ; trusted HOST must bind both to the same immutable capture, target, request and owner.
findings.required_behavior: Save captured R, keep live R+1 dirty, preserve recovery baseline; no UI-supplied digest acknowledgement.
findings.missing: Exact captured-save record, receipt-validation result and postcommit acknowledgement error/late-owner semantics.
findings.recommendation: Propose immutable capture binding with document/session/project/request, captured revision+semantic digest, encoded bytes+raw digest, expected previous raw digest and trusted target. Validate target/raw hashes/previous digest/txid before ACK. ACK only semantic digest from captured content, never raw receipt digest. If disk commit succeeds but ACK cannot apply, preserve persistence proof and report committed/ack-deferred instead of ordinary failed-unchanged.

findings.trigger: Approved S1 has status RecoveryRequired and rejects edits while in that state, but no public transition method exists to enter it from a native IO outcome. Silent state reconstruction or a new setter would change the accepted Skeleton.
findings.required_behavior: Exact RecoveryRequired diagnostics retained and further destructive document operations blocked without losing content/history/baselines.
findings.missing: Approved location/owner of IO safety gate and how its state combines with DocumentSession status.

options.proposal: Proposed per-session HOST IO-health guard owned by existing M04 application/session boundary; all destructive inputs check it before calling S1. Domain content/history status unchanged; projection explicitly combines IO health and domain editability. Requires precise guard lifecycle/DTO scope approval, no global manager.

Explicit new domain transition API and lifecycle contract to enter/resolve RecoveryRequired. Requires S1 public API/Skeleton/TDD revision and Owner adoption; cannot be treated as local implementation.

findings.recommendation: Prefer A for current S2 integration if complete boundary coverage can be proved; present exact model and all-entry guards for one review before Skeleton. Do not self-approve either option.
